problem_statement: Nuxtship is a Nuxt 3 marketing site for a startup deploy platform (a home landing with a hero, feature grid, logo wall and call-to-action; an About page with the team; a Pricing page; and a Contact page, all wrapped by a shared Navbar and Footer under the landing layout). The team wants a small, consistent 'Launch checklist' rail to sit in the footer of every marketing page: a labelled row of the five launch steps (Connect repository, Configure domain, Preview deploy, Ship to production, Watch analytics) plus a live 'Deploy target' readout with a toggle that tells the visitor whether the rail is currently pointed at the staging preview or production — a marketer previews on staging then promotes to production, so the rail should always name the target the toggle is set to. Ship the Launch checklist rail so it (1) appears in the footer on the home, About, Pricing and Contact pages alike, (2) lays out its step row responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches the site's quiet slate/black marketing styling (bordered slate steps, not an off-palette dark slab), and (4) keeps the 'Deploy target' readout in sync with the toggle so a visitor who switches to production sees the readout update to 'production live'. Keep the rest of the site — navigation, existing page content, the static build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Launch checklist' rail to the site footer so it renders on the home, About, Pricing and Contact pages (a shared component invoked from Footer.vue, not a per-page copy).

The rail shows a 'Ship in five steps' label, a step row of the launch steps (Connect repository, Configure domain, Preview deploy, Ship to production, Watch analytics), and a 'Deploy target' readout with a toggle.
The step row must wrap responsively so no marketing page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the rail in the site's quiet slate/black marketing language (bordered slate steps), consistent and legible, not an off-palette dark slab.

Wire the 'Deploy target' readout to the target toggle: give the toggle button id="launch-target-btn" and, after clicking it, the readout must read 'production live' when the rail is set to production — it must re-read the live deploy target, not show a stale captured value.
Preserve navigation (Home/Pricing/About/Contact), the footer, the existing home/About/Pricing/Contact content, the team portraits and the static build with no console or network errors.
author_notes: Built on the Gr33nW33n nuxtship-template Nuxt 3 landing theme (Navbar/Footer shell under the landing layout, Tailwind slate/black palette, local hero and team portrait imagery). The shared Launch checklist rail is rendered from Footer.vue with local image assets; no remote assets are added — the original Unsplash portraits and the web3forms contact endpoint were vendored to local assets so the static build is fully offline.
design_constraints: Implement the Launch checklist rail as a shared component rendered from the footer so a single source of truth reaches every page; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The step row must use a fluid, wrapping responsive layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile; the step spacing must stay legible.
The rail must adopt the site's slate/black palette, bordered-step style and marketing typography so it reads as part of Nuxtship, not a foreign block; keep it consistent with the site's imagery.
The 'Deploy target' readout must reflect the CURRENT deploy target after every toggle by reading the live data-launch-target, so it can never go stale relative to the visible tint.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, existing content, the team portraits, the contact form or the static build.

change_completion: The Launch checklist rail is present in the footer of the home, About, Pricing and Contact pages (the shared component reaches all four routes).
After clicking the target toggle on the home page, the 'Deploy target' readout updates to 'production live' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'staging preview'.
design_consistency: The rail on the footer states matches the reference's slate/black marketing styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-palette dark slab.
The rail adopts the site's slate bordered-step idiom so it reads as part of Nuxtship across the marketing pages.
responsive: No captured marketing page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the step row wraps.
desktop_footer_home, mobile_footer_home and mobile_initial keep the Launch checklist rail readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Navigation (Home/Pricing/About/Contact), the footer and the team portraits remain present and functional.
The existing home/About/Pricing/Contact content and the static Nuxt build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the homepage hero and responsive shell.
desktop_about, mobile_about, desktop_pricing, desktop_contact and mobile_contact protect the existing marketing pages and carry the Launch checklist rail in the footer.
desktop_footer_home and mobile_footer_home scroll the Launch checklist rail into view and must show the slate/black rail without horizontal overflow.
desktop_footer_about and desktop_footer_contact protect the rail's presence on the About and Contact page footers.
toggle_target_home clicks the target toggle; the 'Deploy target' readout must then read 'production live'.
